audit.summary: Archived assessment: Major. Global obstacle representation fails even for natural boundary data; Exact straight cusp rays need not map perpendicularly
limitations: Global obstacle representation fails even for natural boundary data — Scope limit: Specific acquired source and stated local clauses/proof dependencies only; no unsupported main-theorem failure assertion.
Exact straight cusp rays need not map perpendicularly — Counterevidence and scope: The stated O(t³) estimate in (5.35) holds for this example, with a nonzero cubic coefficient.

Exact straight cusp rays need not map perpendicularly — Counterevidence and scope: For every other inward angle in the corollary, the displayed exact identity has nonzero real quadratic coefficient (4cos²θ−3)/9. Thus the general quadratic behavior in part (i) also survives.

Exact straight cusp rays need not map perpendicularly — Counterevidence and scope: A Möbius change from the original disk to a half-plane does not carry these exact straight rays to exact straight rays: a second-order path displacement can modify the cubic coefficient when the quadratic leading term cancels.

Exact straight cusp rays need not map perpendicularly — Counterevidence and scope: The example proves failure of the perpendicular-direction clause in Corollary 5.17(ii). It does not disprove the main Hölder exponents, the Pokrovsky–Talapov law, general transversality, or the universality theorem.

Exact straight cusp rays need not map perpendicularly — Counterevidence and scope: Which later statements require exact orthogonality rather than cubic order or mere transversality remains a parent proof-dependency check.
Exact straight cusp rays need not map perpendicularly — Scope limit: Specific acquired source and stated local clauses/proof dependencies only; no unsupported main-theorem failure assertion.
